summary: Screen climate-exposed assets, assess consequences, and prepare adaptation and disclosure outputs. Explore the five-day course and practical curriculum.
lede: Physical climate risk assessment training helps infrastructure and utility planners evaluate how hazards may affect assets, services, and finances. It is also for climate-risk officers, public finance teams, and insurance professionals who need to prioritize action using asset screening, exposure mapping, vulnerability and service-impact analysis, and scenario comparison. Exercises apply these capabilities to risk registers, adaptation options, financial consequence summaries, and climate-risk disclosure evidence.
audienceIntro: This course is for professionals who assess climate-exposed infrastructure, essential services, investment decisions, or insurance portfolios and need asset-level evidence to guide action.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with infrastructure assets, climate risk, public investment, insurance, or ESG reporting is recommended. No coding or climate-model development is required; basic spreadsheet and digital file-management skills will help with the exercises.
